Subject: Next steps: hosting preference + migration path for MediFin Health

Hi Rajesh / Anika —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and a proposed set of next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (from the discovery call)
- Primary constraint: data residency + PHI handling — your security team prefers private VPC or on-prem for initial rollout.
- Current environment: mix of legacy GPU cluster (on-prem) and a small POC with a third-party LLM API for non-PHI traffic.
- Key metrics: 50–120 TPS at 512 tokens for peak inference, average latency SLO 150ms p95 for critical routes.

Options we discussed
1) Hosted API (fastest to ship) — good for non-PHI routes and hybrid traffic.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) — predictable throughput + isolation, could be in your cloud account or our dedicated tenants.
3) Private VPC / on-prem package — meets compliance/residency but requires longer lead time (networking, KMS, audit integration).

Open questions we need to qualify
- Which routes must never leave your VPC (PHI)?
- Are you willing to run Redwood Private in your cloud (VPC) vs fully on-prem?
- What timeline do you have for decommissioning the legacy GPU cluster?

Proposed next steps
- Rajesh: confirm whether PHI must remain on-prem (reply by EOD Wed).
- Redwood: send a preliminary capacity estimate and migration checklist (attached).
- If PHI must stay in your environment, schedule a technical deep dive with Soojin (solutions eng) to walk through network/KMS requirements.
- Proposed tentative dates for the deep dive: Wed 5/5 or Thu 5/6 (we can accommodate PST/EST).

Attaching: capacity_estimate.xlsx (first-pass numbers).

If that all looks right I’ll schedule the deep dive and loop legal for the initial NDA/SOW friction points.

Thanks,

Logan —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PHI requirement: All patient-identifiable inference must remain in our VPC; we are hesitant to send PHI to any hosted multi-tenant API.
- Cloud vs on-prem: We prefer VPC-first (in our GCP org) but may require a full on-prem install for the pilot environment tied to audits.
- Legacy cluster: The engineering team is looking to keep it for 3–6 months while we validate model parity and latency. We are not planning an immediate lift-and-shift.
- Third-party LLM API: The POC is only for non-PHI routing; we need guidance on dual-routing (some traffic to third-party, critical traffic to private).

We are available for the technical deep dive on Thu 5/6 at 11:00 AM ET. Please include your solutions engineer and any network/security folks who can speak to VPC/KMS integration and audit logging.

— Rajesh

Hi Rajesh —

Thanks — that aligns with what we saw. A few notes from a solutions-engineering perspective ahead of Thu’s deep dive (attached: migration_checklist.pdf):

1) Migration patterns we recommend
  - Hybrid split routing: keep PHI inside your VPC (Redwood Private deployed in your GCP VPC), route non-PHI to Hosted API during validation. This reduces cutover risk and lets you benchmark.
  - Phased lift-and-shift: keep legacy GPU cluster for batch/housekeeping jobs while routing real-time inference to Redwood Dedicated/Private. Plan a 3-month window to validate model parity and autoscaling.
  - API compatibility shim: we provide a small gateway that mimics common LLM API surface (reduces app changes) — helpful when you're validating against a third-party provider.

2) Technical checklist (high level)
  - Network: VPC peering / private interconnect + BGP routes; firewall rules documentation.
  - Auth: KMS/HSM integration for key wrapping; support for customer-managed keys.
  - Audit: streaming audit logs, token-level usage export, retention policy mapping.
  - Data flows: signing/encryption at rest and in transit; clear routing table for PHI vs non-PHI.

3) Inputs we need from your engineering team before the deep dive
  - A sample traffic profile (p95 tokens per request, peak TPS), if you can share.
  - Which endpoints must be PHI-only.
  - Preferred KMS provider (Cloud KMS vs HSM vendor).

I’ll bring a short implementation timeline and an example network diagram to Thu’s call. If you prefer a full on-prem runbook instead, we can scope that too but it will add ~4–6 weeks for packaging and audit prep.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
